candidates.summary: Bloomberg News journalist barred from China meeting after Nvidia question A Bloomberg News journalist was barred from covering the trilateral meeting in China of President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after she asked a question in a prior meeting w
candidates.full: Bloomberg News journalist barred from China meeting after Nvidia question A Bloomberg News journalist was barred from covering the trilateral meeting in China of President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after she asked a question in a prior meeting with Trump and Xi about Nvidia founder Jensen Huang. The reporter was Annmarie Hordern, who is the chief political correspondent for Bloomberg Television and co-host of the program “Bloomberg Surveillance,” according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media. Hordern was “barred” from the event “because she asked a question during the bilateral meeting with Xi,” according to a pool report distributed early Thursday. The report also said that a White House official said they “pushed to have her reinstated but Chinese officials insisted she be excluded.” A White House spokesperson confirmed that account in an email to The Washington Post. Jacqui Heinrich, a Fox News correspondent who is the president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, wrote on X that it is “commendable” that the White House advocated for press access. According to a separate pool report posted on social media by Heinrich, the Bloomberg News reporter asked, “President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?” Huang, the former CEO of Nvidia, resigned after he admitted to having an affair. Huang has not specified who the affair was with, but it is widely reported to be a business associate named Alice Huang, a Chinese-born former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed who U.S. intelligence has speculated may be a spy in the Chinese government’s employ. Another reporter also began to ask a question but was “shushed by Chinese officials,” according to the pool report. “The Chinese have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and we will be pulled from the room if we do so.” A spokeswoman for Bloomberg News declined to comment. Bloomberg News, a major U.S. media company comprising a news service, website, magazines, radio and television networks, has had a testy history with China in recent years. In 2020, a Chinese employee at Bloomberg News named Haze Fan was detained on suspicion of endangering national security. She was released on bail in 2022. In 2013, Bloomberg News faced allegations that it killed a report by a reporter named Michael Forsythe because it was unfavorable to China, where the company had business interests. Cate Cadell contributed to this report. The outages keep coming. Some Americans are preparing for a collapse. candidates.full: Anthropic рассказала, как готовила к запуску свой редактор документов Claude Docs: за две недели до релиза инженер оставил сессию Claude Code, которая без перерыва нагружала тестовый кластер, ломала компоненты, читала телеметрию и сама выкатывала исправления. По словам компании, к 22 сентября, через шесть дней после запуска, пользователи создали больше 4,6 млн документов, на 2 млрд запросов пришлось 60 серверных ошибок, а сервис ни разу не откатывали. Пост в инженерном блоге claude.dev опубликовал 17 ноября инженер Anthropic Вивек Наир. Для разработчика здесь интересен не сам Claude Docs, а рецепт: как поставить ИИ-агенту задачу уровня «сервис должен выдержать запуск», а не «почини этот баг», и что для этого подготовить в коде и инфраструктуре. Автор приводит стоимость всего инференса с конца августа до запуска — около $125 тыс. по прайсу API — и оценку для небольшого сервиса: $3–10 тыс. за двухнедельный прогон. Все цифры в посте — данные самой Anthropic, независимо их не проверить. Claude Docs — редактор, в котором с документом одновременно работают люди и Claude: любая сессия Claude, от чата до Claude Code, может открыть документ, читать, писать и комментировать в реальном времени. Его выпустили 16 сентября 2026 года. За три недели до этого сервис работал прототипом на одном узле, им пользовались несколько тысяч сотрудников Anthropic, а собственная оценка команды обещала миллионы документов в первые дни после запуска. Реального трафика такого масштаба не было, поэтому 4 сентября автор поручил Claude управлять staging-кластером, повторяющим продакшен: генерировать больше миллиона синтетических документов в день и намеренно ломать основные компоненты. Цикл — это одна сессия Claude Code, оставленная работать: выбрать сценарий, запустить нагрузочный стенд, прочитать телеметрию, предложить исправление, выкатить его на staging и повторить. Сессия работала координатором и отдавала большую часть работы субагентам: в самую загруженную неделю обычно около 11 одновременно, на пике 30. Через Slack MCP координатор ещё и общался с внутренней версией Claude Tag — агентами других инфраструктурных команд Anthropic, которые уже масштабировали похожие сервисы и проверяли подход на известные им ловушки. Телеметрию Claude читал через Datadog MCP. Сценарии автор выбирал заведомо «параноидальные»: Каждая итерация выглядела одинаково: стенд доводил одну функцию, например создание документов, до насыщения, а Claude читал телеметрию и возвращался с коротким списком вариантов и рекомендацией. Если изменение легко откатить, Claude писал его, проверял в отдельной сессии и выкатывал на staging, после чего тест запускался снова; на схеме из поста выбор варианта и одобрение изменения остаются за человеком. Каждый запрос к базе отчитывался своим именем и тем, сколько строк он просканировал и сколько вернул, поэтому плохие запросы находились и переписывались сразу. До старта автор перечислил Claude решения, которые требуют его одобрения: всё, что трудно откатить, — изменения схемы базы и раскладки ключей, способа хранения и материализации документа. Встретив такое решение, агент останавливался и спрашивал, обычно с рекомендацией, которую автор в итоге принимал. Про схемы данных он пишет, что разумных ответов обычно несколько, а менять направление потом больно. Кроме того, весь прогон держался на двух инвариантах. Документ должен открываться практически мгновенно, даже с длинной историей правок. И если сервер подтвердил правку, тесты должны показывать, что она сохранилась. По словам автора, модель держала эти инварианты через многократное сжатие контекста, и повторять их не пришлось. Автор ссылается на заметку коллеги Феликса Ризеберга: формулировать задачу на уровне результата («сделай приложение без падений»), а не отдельного действия («почини это падение»). Чтобы это работало, агент должен сам получать отчёты о сбоях и запускать стенд, который воспроизводит сбой и проверяет исправление. Для этого команда сделала две вещи. Первая — диагностический цикл: на каждой итерации Claude читал телеметрию и сам добавлял метрики, которых не хватало. Обычно телеметрию дописывают руками и уже после аварии, здесь агент делал это по ходу работы. Показательный пример — память. В начале прогона один большой документ занимал на поде около 3 ГБ. Первая гипотеза Claude — уменьшить кэш, чтобы сервер раньше выгружал документы, — не подтвердилась: следующий прогон показал, что память сидит в отдельном кэше внутри одной из зависимостей, и правку отменили. Более детальное профилирование нашло причину: каждое нажатие клавиши копировало документ в несколько разных структур данных, добавляя несколько мегабайт. Claude перевёл эти структуры на copy-on-write, чтобы они ссылались на одну копию. Примерно через три дня итераций тот же документ занимал около 180 МБ, а оценка мощности, нужной для запуска, упала с более чем 500 подов с оптимизированной памятью до примерно 50. Весь сервис на запуске и работал примерно на 50 таких подах. Вторая — выбор технологий. Команда избегала рантаймов, которые расходуют память и процессор так, что код этим не управляет, то есть языков со сборщиком мусора: по логике автора, память и задержки в них меняются по расписанию сборщика, а модели лучше всего «карабкаются» по чистому сигналу. Сервис написан на Rust, зависимостей минимум, а немногие нужные библиотеки вендорили, чтобы их можно было читать и измерять. Автор оговаривается: в Anthropic есть хороший инструментарий для Go, и сравнения двух языков команда не проводила — это опыт с Rust, а не тест. Его довод: Rust трудно писать людям, но Claude пишет на нём нормально, поэтому сложность языка теперь весит меньше. По данным Anthropic, первый миллион документов появился примерно за 30 часов после запуска 16 сентября, к 22 сентября их было больше 4,6 млн. На 2 млрд запросов пришлось 60 серверных ошибок. Продакшен в сентябре выкатывали 629 раз, и ни одна выкатка не потребовала отката. Семь из десяти сценариев, отрепетированных на staging, действительно произошли в продакшене. К тому моменту Claude уже выпустил исправления за флагами времени выполнения, поэтому, когда часть инфраструктуры оказывалась под давлением, команда обычно просто включала флаг. Почему это стало возможно только сейчас, автор объясняет «дрейфом цели» (goal drift): старые модели нормально читали телеметрию через MCP, но через 10–20 итераций длинного цикла забывали, что именно оптимизируют, и цель приходилось повторять (подробнее о дрейфе — в другом посте claude.dev). Сам он работал с внутренней исследовательской моделью, которую сравнивает с Claude Fable 5.2. Похожий подход, по словам автора, применила Vercel, которая агентным циклом под присмотром человека ускорила Turborepo: по данным Vercel, подготовка графа задач перед запуском в версии 2.9.0 стала быстрее до 96% по сравнению с 2.8.0, в зависимости от репозитория. С конца августа до дня запуска автор израсходовал инференса примерно на $125 тыс. по прайсу API Claude Fable 5.2 на ноябрь 2026 года. В эту сумму входит вся работа за период, не только нагрузочный цикл; большая часть ушла на чтение телеметрии, предложения, генерацию исправлений и ревью кода. Он сам называет два фактора, которые раздули счёт: масштаб запуска потребовал инфраструктуры, о которой агенту пришлось много рассуждать, а много токенов сгорело, пока он отлаживал сам процесс; сейчас, по его оценке, хватило бы половины. Пару лет назад такая работа, по его догадке, заняла бы у команды инженеров около полугода. Для небольшого сервиса — пара Kubernetes-узлов и Postgres — автор пересчитал затраты, убрав интеграцию с внутренними сервисами, продуктовую работу, работу на множестве подов и тонкий rate limiting. Осталась примерно треть изменений, и двухнедельный прогон, по его оценке, обошёлся бы в $3–10 тыс. по тому же прайсу. Он прямо пишет, что такой прогон не запускал и цифра приблизительная. Рецепт из поста рассчитан на одного инженера с Claude Code, staging-окружение и сервис наблюдаемости: Координатор с субагентами ускорял работу, но автор допускает, что если они сжигают слишком много токенов в час, один агент тоже справится. Это самый простой способ снизить счёт при первом опыте. По нашей оценке, переносимая часть рецепта не зависит от конкретного агента: телеметрия, доступная через MCP, стенд с намеренными сбоями, записанные инварианты и явный список решений, которые остаются за человеком. Без изолированного staging запускать такой цикл нельзя: агент здесь сам выкатывает изменения, и границы его прав нужно продумать заранее — как это делают, мы разбирали в материале про изоляцию агентов. Как подобрать модель и уровень рассуждений под долгую задачу, Anthropic объясняла в отдельном руководстве. Источники: claude.dev: Using a chaos loop to harden the Claude Docs launch, Felix Rieseberg: How to be more ambitious, Vercel: Turborepo на 96% быстрее с агентами, claude.dev: A harness for every task Изображение на обложке: Tproger по данным Anthropic

candidates.full: Бйорн Ульвеус з ABBA задонатив на допомогу Україні понад 100 тисяч євро Бйорн Ульвеус з ABBA задонатив на допомогу Україні понад 100 тисяч євро (Фото: Jack Mikrut (Di)) Співзасновник та учасник легендарного шведського гурту ABBA Бйорн Ульвеус задонатив на підтримку українців взимку понад 100 тисяч євро. Про це повідомили у посольстві України у Швеції. Бйорн Ульвеус приєднався до кампанії посольства України #KeepUkraineWarm (зігрійте Україну), спрямованою на підтримку українців протягом складної п’ятої зими. Він висловив захоплення українським народом і протистоянням російському тирану. «Україна бореться за нас. Ми знаємо, що Путін хотів би захопити Балтику, і тому я думаю, що нам слід було б набагато, набагато, набагато більше підтримувати Україну з самого початку», — зазначив Бйорн Ульвеус в інтерв'ю шведському виданню Dagens industri. Він також зауважив, що допомога американців за Байдена була невпевненою. Ульвеус також пригадав Холодну війну і зауважив, що його завжди лякала перспектива опинитися під радянським ярмом. «Ми так близько до Балтії, яка на той час була радянською. Ця загроза не полишила мене. Я пам’ятаю, як у молодості думав: «Я б краще помер, ніж жив під таким комуністичним ярмом», — поділився він. Ульвеус від початку повномасштабного вторгнення Росії в Україну у 2022 році займає активну позицію на підтримку України. Він неодноразово закликав міжнародну спільноту до пожертвувань на користь краудфандингової ініціативи United24, а долучитися донатом до нової ініціативи він вирішив після зустрічі із послом України у Швеції Світланою Заліщук, яка розповіла, що головним пріоритетом на зиму є забезпечення генераторами та опаленням цивільного населення. Він також зауважив, що хотів би якось відвідати Україну, в якій раніше не був. Кошти, зібрані під час кампанії #KeepUkraineWarm, будуть спрямовані на придбання генераторів для дошкільних закладів, шкіл та дитячих лікарень.

candidates.summary: Новий гаджет Apple майже неможливо відремонтувати: що з ним не так Новий гаджет Apple майже неможливо відремонтувати: що з ним не так Фахівці iFixit виявили, що новий пристрій Apple HomeView має конструкційні особливості, які значно ускладнюють його ремонт. Зокрема, алюмінієвий корпус і міцний кле
candidates.full: Новий гаджет Apple майже неможливо відремонтувати: що з ним не так Новий гаджет Apple майже неможливо відремонтувати: що з ним не так Фахівці iFixit виявили, що новий пристрій Apple HomeView має конструкційні особливості, які значно ускладнюють його ремонт. Зокрема, алюмінієвий корпус і міцний клей ускладнюють демонтаж дисплея, а надмірно закріплені клеєм кабелі підключення динаміків пошкоджуються під час розбирання. Материнська плата також закріплена великою кількістю термоклею, що потребує використання різних типів гвинтів для демонтажу компонентів. Фахівці iFixit розібрали новий пристрій Apple HomeView і звернули увагу на кілька несподіваних особливостей його конструкції. Деякі з них ускладнили навіть звичайне розбирання гаджета. Демонтаж дисплея потребував додаткових зусиль через алюмінієвий корпус і міцний клей, який утримує екран. Під час розбирання пошкодилися кабелі підключення динаміків: їх надмірно закріпили клеєм. Материнську плату також утримує велика кількість термоклею, а для демонтажу різних компонентів потрібні кілька типів гвинтів. На материнській платі виявили процесор Apple A18, 8 ГБ оперативної пам'яті LPDDR5X від SK Hynix і флешпам'ять Kioxia NAND обсягом 64 ГБ. Проблеми виникли й під час демонтажу антен та динаміків: їх також закріпили клеєм, тому для вилучення компонентів довелося докладати значних зусиль. Нагадаємо, що iFixit показала, чому нові Apple Watch досі складно ремонтувати. iFixit виявив слабке місце Galaxy Fold 8, яке може стати проблемою і для складаного iPhone. candidates.full: 🧠 Агенты у вас уже прижились. Кто поведёт изменения в команде? В посте про тест Матущака я признался: самая полезная моя база - служебная. На ней держатся серверы школы, оплаты, рассылка и работа над контентом, а читают её в основном агенты. Перед любой правкой они обязаны найти похожий сбой или прошлое решение. Пока система личная, всё просто: правила для агентов пишет один человек, и проверяет, что агент сделал, тоже он. Когда общий контекст ведет не человек, а компания, острые вопросы переезжают в координацию. что отдать агенту, в каких точках проверять, кто принимает результат и что делать, когда агент ошибся. Если внедрение никто не ведёт, агенты приживаются у одного сотрудника, который разобрался лучше всех. Остальные перепроверяют руками каждое решение, очередь растёт, а общая база превращается в мёртвую, в которую страшно заходить. Как вопрос координации людей и агентов решили другие команды, что на пару шагов впереди, разберут в этот четверг на открытой конференции «Агенты изменений» от AI Mindset - ребят, у которых я сам проходил лаборатории. План на 3 часа: *️⃣ Степан Гершуни, основатель венчурного фонда cyber.fund, - 5 стадий AI-native компании: на какой ваша и что нужно для следующей. *️⃣ Александр Поваляев, фаундер AI Mindset, - AI-native команда изнутри: что делают агенты, что люди и кто за что отвечает. *️⃣ Живой разбор кейсов участников - где внедрение обычно ломается. Кода и настройки не будет, три часа про роли, проверки и процессы. На выходе - понимание, с чего начать трансформацию в своей команде, какие задачи отдать агенту уже завтра и куда двигаться дальше. 19 ноября, 20-23 мск, онлайн, бесплатно 👉 регистрация тут #SecondBrain #AI #PKM #ДмитрийЛаухин

candidates.summary: Constructorul german Mercedes-Benz a prezentat noile funcții MB.Drive, care permit condusul fără mâini pe volan la viteze de autostradă și inițierea automată a manevrelor de depășire, anunță La Repubblica. Noile sisteme permit rularea fără mâini pe volan pe autostradă la viteze de până la 130 km/h ș
candidates.full: Constructorul german Mercedes-Benz a prezentat noile funcții MB.Drive, care permit condusul fără mâini pe volan la viteze de autostradă și inițierea automată a manevrelor de depășire, anunță La Repubblica. Noile sisteme permit rularea fără mâini pe volan pe autostradă la viteze de până la 130 km/h și execută automat schimbarea benzilor pentru depășiri sau navigație, fără confirmarea manuală a șoferului. Tehnologia va debuta în Germania până la finalul anului 2026, urmând să ajungă în SUA în 2027, și va putea fi activată de la distanță inclusiv pe modelele compatibile aflate deja pe șosele. Deși conducătorul auto rămâne responsabil să supravegheze permanent traficul, sistemele oferă o asistență continuă de la plecare până la destinație și vor putea fi descărcate ca actualizări software directe chiar și pe vehiculele deja cumpărate. Își fac astfel debutul Hands-free assist și Proactive lane change assist, două tehnologii concepute să funcționeze împreună, completate de sistemul Mb.Drive Assist Pro, capabil să însoțească șoferul pe întreg traseul, de la plecare până la destinația finală, inclusiv pe tronsoanele urbane. Atunci când condițiile de conducere o permit, sistemul Hands-free Assist permite șoferului să-și ia mâinile de pe volan pe autostradă până la o viteză de 130 km/h, adaptând viteza la fluxul traficului. Pentru a face deplasarea și mai fluidă, sistemul Proactive Lane Change Assist inițiază și execută în mod autonom schimbările de bandă fără a solicita confirmarea manuală a șoferului, fie pentru a depăși un vehicul mai lent, fie pentru a urma indicațiile sistemului de navigație către ieșirea corectă. Cu toate acestea, responsabilitatea șoferului rămâne neschimbată, acesta fiind obligat să supravegheze constant drumul pentru a prelua controlul în orice moment. Introducerea se va face treptat pe întreaga gamă de autoturisme și autoutilitare ale mărcii cu steaua, începând cu Germania până la sfârșitul anului 2026, pentru a se extinde apoi în Statele Unite în cursul anului 2027. Pe vehiculele compatibile aflate deja în circulație, aceste funcții vor putea fi activate chiar și după achiziție, printr-o actualizare software convenabilă de tip „over-the-air”, conform modalităților și prețurilor care vor fi comunicate la momentul lansării. © G4Media.ro.

candidates.full: «Не хотіли ризикувати»: Забарний оцінив важку перемогу збірної України над Грузією в Лізі націй Ілля Забарний (Фото: УАФ) Захисник збірної України Ілля Забарний прокоментував перемогу над Грузією (1:0) у Лізі націй. Футболіст визнав, що після швидкого голу Данила Сікана на першій хвилині українська команда свідомо вирішила грати обережніше. «Дуже важка перемога. Грузія створювала моменти, виглядала непогано. Дмитро [Різник] виручив, адже ми могли пропустити. Радий, що все склалося саме так. Рухаємося далі. Коли забиваєш швидкий м’яч, гра трохи змінюється. До того ж у центрі поля був не надто якісний газон, тому ми не хотіли зайвий раз ризикувати й намагалися більше виходити в атаку через фланги. Забили швидкий м’яч, тому потрібно було діяти обережніше, бо всі розуміють: якщо пропустиш, то забивати буде дуже важко", — сказав Забарний в ефірі Megogo. Захисник також відзначив самовіддачу збірної України, але наголосив, що команді ще потрібно прогресувати й краще грати на третині поля суперника. «Сьогодні — молодці. Вважаю, що ми викладалися на максимум і робили все, щоб перемогти. Приємно вигравати, хочеться перемагати в кожній грі, але є над чим працювати. Попереду в нас важкі матчі, і всі це розуміють. Потрібно додавати у вольових якостях і якості гри. Ми добре контролюємо м’яч, але треба створювати більше моментів», — підсумував Забарний. Нагадаємо, команда Андреа Мальдери фінішувала третьою в групі ліги В і залишилася у дивізіоні на наступний сезон. Українці розпочали турнір із виїзної перемоги над Угорщиною (1:0) та нічиєї з Грузією (0:0). Однак згодом зазнали трьох поразок поспіль: від Північної Ірландії (0:3, 0:1) та Угорщини (1:2). Завершити виступи в групі вдалося перемогою над Грузією. Повідомлялось, що Данило Сікан став автором найшвидшого голу в історії збірної України в офіційних матчах.

candidates.full: Художники способны интуитивно создавать изображения, надолго остающиеся в памяти зрителей. Это подтвердил эксперимент Чикагского университета, во время которого художники сознательно создавали незабываемые и легко забываемые работы. Художники могут интуитивно понимать, какие визуальные особенности помогают изображениям оставаться в памяти. К такому выводу пришли исследователи Чикагского университета, организовавшие художественный конкурс и попросившие участников создать работы, которые должны быть либо максимально запоминаемыми, либо, наоборот, легко забывать. В течение трех месяцев ученые собрали 86 работ, отвечающих условиям конкурса. Сначала их показали участникам онлайн-эксперимента. Выяснилось, что картины, отнесенные художниками к категории незабываемых, действительно лучше откладывались в памяти. В то же время более простые изображения, с меньшим количеством повторяющихся элементов и более низким уровнем симметрии, запоминались лучше. После этого исследователи отобрали 40 работ — 20 самых и 20 наименее запоминаемых — и организовали выставку в галерее Чикаго. Посетители могли свободно осматривать экспозицию, а затем ученые проверяли, какие картины они смогли вспомнить. Результат повторился: работы, хорошо запоминающиеся во время онлайн-тестирования, так же отличались в реальном пространстве. Причем эффект проявлялся даже после нескольких минут просмотра. Отдельно команда проверила, могут ли люди и искусственный интеллект предвидеть, какие изображения лучше всего запомнятся. Для этого использовали нейросеть ResMem, созданную специально для прогнозирования запоминаемости изображений. Она продемонстрировала самые лучшие результаты, опередив художников и обычных пользователей интернета. Интересно, что модель раньше училась только на фотографиях, а не на оригинальных художественных работах. По мнению авторов, эти результаты свидетельствуют о том, что художники могут быть ценными партнерами в исследованиях человеческой памяти. Анализ их творческих решений поможет выяснить, какие визуальные характеристики облегчают запоминание. Усовершенствованные алгоритмы типа ResMem потенциально пригодятся не только художникам и дизайнерам выставок, но и педагогам. В частности, их можно использовать для создания учебных материалов, помогающих детям и пациентам лучше усваивать сложную информацию. Результаты исследования были опубликованы в журнале Psychological Science.

candidates.full: «Мій найголовніший сержант». Мадяр привітав дружину Наталію зі святом і показав спільне фото Роберт Бровді (Фото: robert_madyar в Instagram) Роберт Бровді із позивним Мадяр привітав свою дружину-військову Наталію із Днем сержанта ЗСУ. Він показав спільне фото із нею та назвав її позивний. Командувач Сил безпілотних систем ЗСУ Роберт Бровді з позивним Мадяр привітав українських військових із Днем сержанта. Це свято відзначають 18 листопада. Він також показав спільне фото із дружиною Наталією Бровді, яка має таке звання. «Мій найголовніший сержант Крила. Лідерство, емпатія, опора солдата та незламна воля. Значущість, що набула на війні інших сенсів. З Днем сержанта Збройних Сил України!», — мовиться у підписі. Мадяр також додав, що Україна вистоїть та згадав у дописі про Крим. «Ми встоїмо. Крим відбудуємо та відгодуємо», — наголосив він. Зауважимо, що цю заяву він зробив на тлі ураження Кримського мосту, яке відбулося в ніч на 17 листопада. Раніше Мадяр повідомляв про участь СБС в ударі по об'єкту російських окупантів на півострові. Нагадаємо, що у червні Мадяр відсвяткував 30-ту річницю весілля зі своєю дружиною Наталією. Тоді він зворушливо звернувся до коханої, назвавши її «берегинею та крилами» їхнього підрозділу. Мадяр також розповів, що Наталія із позивним Крила прибула у підрозділ 22 червня 2022 року, а вже восени була мобілізована та увійшла до складу на той час ще тактичної групи.

candidates.full: Физики из США впервые успешно провели квантовую верификацию местопребывания, использовав запутанные фотоны и ограничение скорости света. Технология надежно привязывает цифровую безопасность к физической локации и блокирует попытки взлома. Современная цифровая безопасность часто уязвима перед злоумышленниками, которые могут перехватить управление финансовыми операциями или критической инфраструктурой. Команда ученых Национального института стандартов и технологий США под руководством физика Кристера Шалма нашла способ надежно привязать права доступа к реальному физическому пространству. Результаты их эксперимента были опубликованы в журнале Nature. Для проверки метода квантовой верификации местопребывания (QPV) исследователи обустроили в кампусе NIST в Колорадо две станции на расстоянии 195 метров друг от друга, соединив их оптическими волокнами и кабелями. Между ними разместили контрольный терминал. Один из верификаторов генерировал пару квантово запутанных фотонов — частиц света, свойства которых остаются неразрывно связанными на любом расстоянии. Один фотон оставался на станции, другой направлялся к пользователю, чью локацию проверяли. Обе станции одновременно посылали случайные числа, с помощью которых система должна была определить поляризацию полученного фотона и мгновенно вернуть результат. Эту процедуру повторяли миллионы раз. Поскольку ничто во Вселенной не двигается быстрее света, любая попытка мошенника ответить с другого места привела бы к задержке сигнала. В то же время законы квантовой механики делают невозможным незаметное копирование частиц, а успешное прохождение теста Белла гарантирует отсутствие манипуляций. По словам физика Скотта Гленси, практическое внедрение технологии в банках, медицине или на атомных электростанциях займет более десяти лет, поскольку требует развития масштабных квантовых сетей. Однако разработка уже открывает путь к абсолютной защите от удаленных кибератак и телефонного мошенничества.

candidates.title: AI Came for the Coders. Understanding Why Tells Us Who's Next
candidates.summary: I used to joke that I got my degree in poetry instead of computer engineering so that, in case this computing fad went south, I would have something to fall back on. candidates.full: I used to joke that I got my degree in poetry instead of computer engineering so that, in case this computing fad went south, I would have something to fall back on. Thanks to AI, it’s barely a joke anymore. Software engineering, where I’ve spent a good part of the last 25 years of my career, is undergoing a crisis of faith. True believers in the beauty of hand-written code have had it wrested from them. Those who like solving problems and making things with technology, code or no, have been given new toys to play with and tools to master. I liken it to carpentry from the 19th century onward, when jack planes, chisels and hand saws gave way to power sanders, routers, and table saws. The industry scaled, and now ordinary people can afford decent furniture. But there was another cost. The straightforward nature of physical automation If you were happy to become a machine operator instead of a craftsman, you were in business. However, if you fell in love with thin ribbons of wood from a hand plane catching the light, about the only remaining way to make a living now is by filming your craft and becoming an influencer for nostalgic hobbyists. We embraced the automation of manual labour as it led to benefits for many, in affordable goods and free time. We devalued craftsmanship in the bargain. Working at a desk became more respected than making a desk. But when the work of smart coders gets rocked this hard, fear ripples through the desk worker world. If such intellectual work is vulnerable, then what, and who, is next? A comforting but wrong answer is that the “human” stuff is safe, and coding is technical. A much better way to understand what human skills will endure AI automation is to look at a principle as old as machine learning, and one that goes a long way toward explaining what can and cannot be automated by AI. It hasn’t changed since the 50s, and is unlikely to be broken anytime soon. It is easy enough to understand, yet what it predicts can be counterintuitive. So many wrong assumptions, and so much baseless fear-mongering, stem from misunderstanding the nature of AI automation’s natural trajectory. The counterintuitive nature of digital automation In aid of my language studies, I recently created a clone of my voice to help with pronunciation. It took a few hours and about $5 of computing credits to retrain a free open-source model, which now runs locally on my MacBook, entirely within my control. I used it to record one of my AI explainer videos, and played it for my wife, a professional musician with a great sensitivity to voice, who has lived with me for nearly 25 years. She couldn’t tell it wasn’t me. Making art, writing poems and songs, and recognising the face or voice of a loved one feel like inherently human activities. Some of it, like facial recognition, has gone the way computer scientist Larry Tesler predicted: “Intelligence is whatever machines haven’t done yet”. The term “intelligent” didn’t stick to it for long. It has just become a part of everyday life. The ones that feel most like “us”, though, such as art, writing, speaking, and even code, have shaken our sense of identity when done by a machine. Here the AI label stuck fast. Machines doing work we identify with causes us to project our self-image of intelligence onto them as well. Yet AI can also appear incredibly dumb. Researchers who study AI at work have a name for the lopsided progress of AI across disciplines: the jagged frontier.1 It turns out the line between what the machines do well and what they do badly runs nowhere near the line between what we find hard and what we find easy. The frontier only looks ragged because we are measuring it by how “human” the work feels, which means some disciplines and even industries won’t “just catch up” to the outer edge anytime soon. The truth is, speech synthesis and everything else we either take for granted or fear will bring about our obsolescence all conform to the laws of what AI can automate well. These are rules that follow from how machines “learn”, which is also a purely anthropomorphic metaphor. Understanding what can be automated The first AI programmes of the 1950s were specified with rules of reasoning written by hand. The ones that learned arrived in the same decade, among them a programme at IBM that improved at draughts by playing against earlier versions of itself.2 Learning needs something more than just design; it needs a way to keep score. This is why AI plays games so well, eventually surpassing us in finding the best way to win. AI researcher Jason Wei coined “verifier’s law”: the easier a task is to check, the easier it is to train AI to do it. Andrej Karpathy distinguishes the old way of doing software as what you can specify and the new way as what you can verify.3 A digital recording of a voice, it turns out, is easy to check, and easy to verify against the reference voice being cloned. For simplicity, I have bundled all of the elements that Wei and others have identified as necessary for checking and verifying, such as having a right answer, being able to score it reliably, and being able to automate it with sufficient computing power to do it over and over again at high speed, into the term “grading”. All components are necessary to perform AI automation today. But even as data and computing power become more available, at the end of the day some numerical form of analysis, and some evaluation of “correctness”, are make-or-break factors in what can (ever) be graded. Grading, however, is only part of what predicts AI automation. The other part is value, and our agreement on what valuable means. Plotting work along these two dimensions gives us four boxes to consider. Software is among the most-graded work humans have ever produced. It compiles or it doesn’t, the tests pass or they fail, and the automated testing takes seconds on ordinary machines. As long as it’s fit for purpose, nobody disputes that working software is worth having, which puts code in the top-right box. My cloned voice sits beside it. It either passes the wife test or it doesn’t. Yet, as I have said before, there will never be a compiler that can check for bugs in your poem. You can clone a poet’s style, and follow all conventions of form just right. But poetry’s greatest trick is evading mediocrity, which is precisely what endless iterations of numerical comparison and adjustment converge upon. Form and style can be graded; whether the poem is any good cannot. That puts poetry in the bottom-right box. I did a whole talk on it, if you want to hear more. From the standpoint of society, parenting is perhaps the most important job in the world. Grading it automatically (or at all) seems absurd, not least of all because it can take years, even generations, to see the results, which are themselves often easy to recognise but hard to quantify. It sits top left, high in value but beyond grading. The last box holds work that can be neither graded nor valuated objectively. Our carpenters who became hobbyist woodworkers got put in this box by the physical machinery of automation, yet now remain immune to digital automation as a result. Like poetry, the value of the product is a matter of taste, and taste diverges, eluding quantification. Predicting what will be automated Beyond coding, the automation of art and writing feels like the solution to a “problem” that almost nobody wanted to be solved.4 So much of what has been automated most of us lament, and so much of what has not been automated we begrudge. This is because the possibilities of AI automation do not follow our wishes, but follow the principles of automated grading versus objective value outlined above. It also doesn’t matter how “human” it feels: if it scores high on both, it’s possible. This doesn’t make it probable, however. It just shows us where to rule out the impossible. What makes it probable is market incentive. This is different from being able to agree on objective value. This is about capitalism, and the dream of owning the means of production not only for labour, but for knowledge work. For a few decades, a creative with a laptop owned their own means of production, which is more than any mill hand ever could. AI that cranks out marketing imagery on demand hands those means back to whoever pays for the subscription, with only a small amount of remaining work required to publish it and finish the job. Commercial art and writing are in this category. A brief and a paying client supply value agreement, and steady income, that fine art lacks. AI is automating creative commercial work, which means that artists will find it harder to make a living using the same skills as their fine art or literary practice. I must point out, though, that rarely throughout history has anyone who wants to make a living in fine arts been able to do so easily. Van Gogh lived on an allowance from his brother, and a great many famous artists lived on their inheritance. The nepo-baby is a timeless tradition. For the last century or so, there were also side-hustles and day jobs: Warhol drew shoe advertisements, Hopper illustrated magazines, Rushdie wrote advertising copy, and Hemingway and Orwell worked as journalists. Practicing art-making commercially to hone skills, and to cover the rent while doing so, is what is really under threat in the AI age. My own qualitative estimate of how artists and writers have lived without a second profession.5 For most illustrators, copywriters, and translators, of course, the commercial work was never a rehearsal for something higher. It was the job. In a Society of Authors survey, a quarter of illustrators and over a third of translators said they had already lost work to generative AI.6 For them, the option on offer is, like the carpenters of old, to become a machine operator. Re-skilling for the AI age In knowledge work, AI produces deliverables; people achieve outcomes. A deliverable is a thing you can hand over: the report, the code, the slide deck, the campaign image. An outcome is what the thing was for in the first place, such as a presentation you give to the board or a sales deal you close. It only happens when other people agree, adopt, and follow through with complex social interactions. Many deliverables can be graded, which is why AI keeps getting better at those that can. Parenting, by contrast, is a complex set of outcomes, each unarguably valuable yet all ungradeable. Then there is the question of accountability. When things go wrong, a model has no neck to choke. However, if you get fired for work you did with AI, your replacement will sit in the same office chair and use the same AI subscription plan. Capitalism keeps people answerable with an existential threat: if you don’t work, you don’t eat. It operates a long way below a craftsman’s pride in their work. But it operates, like a machine. Markets, after all, have their own intelligence to them. In light of these forces at work, everything outside of what can and will be automated should be the focus of our modern skilling, in both institutional and corporate education. Equally important is to understand how to use AI automations to enhance the value of the outcomes we achieve, and indeed the lives we lead. For an individual, that means a few good habits: decide what the outcome is before requesting the deliverables; check what comes back as though your name were on it (because it will be!); stay close enough to the work that you can verify it is both correct and fit for purpose. I have developed these research-led practices into a method called DRIVE. School grading teaches us everything can be measured, which is why we’re terrified of failing. Objective measures make schooling scalable, and therefore readily available (like furniture), but at the expense of the intangibles now most valuable in the AI era: personal story, big-picture creative thinking, wise judgment, unshakeable ethics, and the ability to struggle in order to learn. I made the case for struggle in particular in Knowing the Answer Was Never the Point. Collectively, the work is to stop valuing ourselves only in relation to what can be graded. Schools must spend less time on grades as a proxy for having learned, and more time on learning how to learn and think in itself. Employers must keep taking on beginners, and treating them like future leaders, lest they have none to choose from in the next decade.7 Those who gain most from AI automation must share what they discover. Learning from one another about AI, ourselves, and our values can give us back the feeling of being a team. Hope? Really? Nearly all anti-AI arguments I have come across use AI as a flashpoint for lamenting the polarisation of wealth, and the capture of knowledge work. The grievance is real; the technology is where it shows most sharply, because it hits us where it hurts, in our intellectual identity. As a coder and creative, I’ve been gut-punched twice; you would think I’d be anything but hopeful about the future. My optimism comes from understanding what AI can and cannot automate, where beyond the tool itself late capitalism has a part in all this mess, and of necessity: my nephews will inherit an AI-native world. I want to do everything I can to be a force for good in bridging us into a future where we are appropriately refocused on using AI intelligently, safely, and well for the benefit of all. Meanwhile the poetry stays where it has always belonged, in my back pocket. - Fabrizio Dell’Acqua and colleagues, Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier, Organization Science 37(2), first circulated in 2023: a field experiment with 758 consultants at Boston Consulting Group. ↩︎ - The designed programme was Logic Theorist (Newell, Shaw, and Simon, 1956). The one that learned was Arthur Samuel’s, described in “Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers” (1959), the paper that popularised the term machine learning. ↩︎ - Jason Wei, Asymmetry of verification and verifier’s rule (2025). Andrej Karpathy, Verifiability (2025). ↩︎ - Stanford’s WORKBank audit asked 1,500 workers about 844 tasks across 104 occupations between January and May 2025. Workers welcomed automation on 46.1% of those tasks overall, and on 17.1% in arts, design, and media. These are shares of tasks, not of people. ↩︎ - The chart is informed guesswork throughout, checked against surveys only for its last two decades. Read it for its shape. The Church gave way to secular patrons, patrons to the open market, and the market to commercial creative work, shown in orange, which by my estimate has carried art practice for about 140 years. Two surveys sit behind its right-hand edge. Arts Council England’s Livelihoods of Visual Artists (2018) asked 2,007 artists in March 2016 about their income in 2015: 90% said their art practice did not earn them enough to live on, and almost seven in ten had another job. The UK authors’ earnings survey found the share of professional authors living on writing alone fell from 40% in 2006 to 19% in 2022. ↩︎ - Society of Authors survey, January 2024, 787 responses: 26% of illustrators and 36% of translators. A separate study of about 1.4 million freelance job posts found that writing and coding posts fell 21% against manual-skill posts in the eight months after ChatGPT launched, and image-creation posts fell 17% (Demirci, Hannane, and Zhu, Management Science, 2025). ↩︎ - Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar, and Ruyu Chen, Canaries in the Coal Mine?, August 2026 revision, from US payroll records to June 2026. Employment for workers aged 22 to 25 in the occupations most exposed to AI runs about 19% below where it would be had it kept pace with their peers in less exposed work, mostly because fewer are being hired. The authors stress that this is a pattern in the data and does not prove AI caused it. ↩︎

candidates.title: Expect a year of accelerating technological progress in AI - The Economist
candidates.summary: Expect a year of accelerating technological progress in AI But also expect growing financial strain By Alex Hern, AI correspondent, The Economist F or years, people have made strange, crazy-sounding predictions about artificial intelligence. It will solve climate change, cure all disease and make
candidates.full: Expect a year of accelerating technological progress in AI But also expect growing financial strain By Alex Hern, AI correspondent, The Economist F or years, people have made strange, crazy-sounding predictions about artificial intelligence. It will solve climate change, cure all disease and make people immortal! It will turn the whole world into paper clips! It will be so advanced that it will treat humans like pets! It was easy to dismiss such speculation with a shrug or an eye-roll. But in 2026 ai actually started to do strange, crazy-sounding things. In several separate incidents, swarms of ai agents went rogue, breaking out of ai labs and breaching external systems. Crypto wallets were drained, and supermarket fridges across Europe set to defrost, in ai-assisted cyber-attacks. ai models produced solutions to long-standing problems in maths, computer science and fluid dynamics, causing much soul-searching in academia. ai-written stories won literary prizes. ai-generated music topped the charts. Suddenly, the risk that progress in ai could lead to unexpected and often frightening outcomes seems much more plausible. Things may seem strange enough already. But in 2027 they will get even stranger. One reason is that ai, already superhuman at coding, hacking and maths, may be about to become far more powerful. Many in the industry expect 2027 to herald the arrival of “recursive self-improvement” (rsi): the process whereby ai systems meaningfully improve their own successors, in a feedback loop that leads to an explosion in ai capabilities. Some worry that crossing this threshold will cause mankind to lose control of the technology, as it starts to improve itself in ways humans cannot comprehend. And rsi could cause havoc in science, as ai models derive new results that baffle humans, as is already happening in maths. When it comes to cyber-security, the loss of control may already have occurred. In early 2026 Anthropic said its most powerful internal model, Mythos, was too dangerous to release openly. As 2027 dawns, those capabilities have proliferated. Open-source models such as Kimi k3 from Moonshot, a Chinese lab, are capable of finding and exploiting cyber-security flaws that were once the preserve of America’s national champions, with little ability to control who has access to that power. At an ai conference in 2026, a majority of leaders in the industry said they expected a cyber-security incident costing $100bn, or 10,000 lives, to happen in the next few years. In theory, ai will improve cyber-security, by allowing engineers to analyse software, and find and patch flaws, before it is released. In practice, there is a lot of old, vulnerable software out in the world already. Vendors are rushing to issue security updates: Microsoft, which used to issue 70-80 patches per month, issued 972 in September and 1,411 in October. But not all software is actively maintained, and not all patches are applied (think of all those supermarket fridges). So the tide of cyber-attacks will rise in the coming months. The ai industry faces a testing and volatile year in other respects, too. A popular and regulatory backlash against data centres is intensifying, threatening the construction of new infrastructure and spooking investors. Anthropic’s public offering will expose its finances to scrutiny; Openai is expected to follow. And the labs face financial pressure on two fronts. First, spending on r&d shows no sign of slowing. The huge cost of training runs is being exacerbated by expensive “post-training” in which ai models’ abilities are honed. If rsi kicks in, those abilities will surge, but so will costs: ai software engineers can spend money on computing power far more quickly than any human. No wonder that, according to Anthropic’s prospectus, released in October, the company expects to spend $750bn on computing power in the coming years. At the same time, the big American labs face growing pricing pressure. Competition from Chinese ai labs has forced them to cut their prices, and the fight is far from over. In October DeepSeek, a Chinese lab, made the software for running its models available free online, to help users run ai models on their own hardware rather than paying for cloud-based services. Running ai models on desktop machines is largely a hobby for now. But researchers at Stanford University found that small ai models were just as good as cloud-based models for over 80% of tasks. For many users, a free, local model running on their laptop or smartphone may be good enough within a year or two—a nightmare scenario for the big American labs. But it would be good news for users of ai. With costs pushed down by competitive pressure, and capabilities continuing to improve thanks to pre-committed investment, the outcome could resemble the explosion in connectivity powered by the telecoms boom at the turn of the millennium. That boom did not, of course, end well for the telecoms companies themselves. The story of the past five years of the ai industry has been of expectations and valuations soaring, as reality struggled to keep up. In 2027 prepare for the opposite: as ai systems start to change the world, in increasingly strange ways, the collective suspension of disbelief may come to an end. ■ This article appeared in the Leaders section of the print edition of The World Ahead 2027 under the headline “Artificial intelligence’s strange new reality” Energy markets are not going back to the way they were, says Fatih Birol The Iran war has changed attitudes, says the head of the International Energy Agency The U-2 Dragon Lady’s time may at last be up The Pentagon has requested no funding for the spy plane in 2027 African film and television are going global The world is finally paying attention to the continent’s talent Christian content will be on screens everywhere in 2027 Museums reckon with the past decade’s cultural shifts

candidates.title: Running two PSP emulators on one Switch 2 and sharing one via GameShare
candidates.summary: This branch experiments with a separate PPSSPP guest running on the host Switch 2 and streamed to a stock GameShare client. It is not a mirrored controller or a second PSP controller in the host emulator. Compilation and host tests do not establish console operation or acceptable two-game performanc
candidates.full: This branch experiments with a separate PPSSPP guest running on the host Switch 2 and streamed to a stock GameShare client. It is not a mirrored controller or a second PSP controller in the host emulator. Compilation and host tests do not establish console operation or acceptable two-game performance. The working single-instance checkpoint is switch2-single-instance-working (commit 1c3b38a). Its exact tested NRO, package and matching debug ELF remain under dist-switch2/checkpoints/switch2-single-instance-working/. sh Tools/build-switch2-gameshare.sh python3 Tools/deploy-switch2.py 192.168.1.182 --experimental-gameshare Open FTPD for the second command. A successful transfer is accepted without a validation download. The experiment installs as PPSSPP GameShare, at sdmc:/switch/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare.nro. It leaves the working ppsspp-switch2 NRO and its settings/saves in place. The normal Tools/build-switch2.sh selects GameShare OFF. Both builds reuse the build cache, but packaging rejects mismatched native/experimental modes. Launch through the same GameShare-capable native title override used for the Moonlight SDK example. A generic title override is not known to grant the required GameShare context. If another title locks profile switching, the SDK uses the Nintendo profile selected for that launch when available. The host log distinguishes a missing launch profile from a later StreamPlay or matchmaking error. Choose GameShare (experimental) in the host's main or pause menu, then join from the client's system GameShare screen. The client should see its own PPSSPP menu, with a guest-only startup message, and browse sdmc:/switch/ppsspp-switch2/games. Both browsers can access SD-card games; no game files are copied into the package. Choose the same GameShare action to stop sharing. The guest pauses between sessions, retaining its independent emulator state. Exiting the guest's PPSSPP ends that guest instance; restart the application before creating another. Exit the host normally when done. If a real cleanup failure reports retained resources, close the entire hosting title from HOME, rather than returning to hbmenu. The SDK explicitly requires this for uncertain native ownership. The build links a second PPSSPP frontend/core into a relocatable object and renames every defined core-owned global symbol and ELF COMDAT group signature. Only eight plain-data C entry points are exported. The audit requires distinct Config, memory-base and core-state symbols; the host also compares their runtime addresses before starting. SDK/OS/C++ runtime entry points remain shared. The two emulators have independent core, UI, filesystem state, JIT registries, Vulkan contexts and settings/memory-stick directories. They share one OS process, so a fatal error in either copy can still affect the entire app. The host keeps its 1920x1080 output and 120 Hz request. The guest uses PPSSPP's existing offscreen Vulkan path at 1280x720 with a 60 fps presentation target. A readback callback transfers completed RGBA frames to a latest-frame mailbox; a dedicated presenter uploads them to a separate native VI2 guest layer. This first route adds CPU readback/swizzle cost; zero-copy is not claimed. The GameShare SDK is vendored from Moonlight-Switch's research worktree. Switch/GameShare/sdk-provenance.json records the source revision and file hashes. Its MIT license and per-file ISC notices are retained. The SDK's pinned CPU-console uploader is disabled. The guest renderer borrows the statically linked OunceVK driver's GSV main and worker sessions and uses its registered VM. It owns the guest image backing, registrations and client. The adapter tracks the driver's occupied slots at the libounce call boundary and reserves a free slot for guest range retirement. Each GameShare session reuses the reserved slot's completion event, which closes with the Vulkan driver's GPU. It does not access OunceVK's internal structs. Retire the guest images before Vulkan teardown. Coexistence and reuse on hardware still require qualification. The SDK owns matchmaking, native hosting, controller reads and the separate VI2 display/layer. Renderer retirement runs before native Finalize; layer closure runs afterwards. Uncertain presentation or release/retirement failure retains backing and blocks ordinary unload. Guest controls never enter the host emulator. Stale/disconnected snapshots become neutral. Host settings/saves use ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/config/ppsspp; guest settings/saves use ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/guest/config/ppsspp. The existing working app's memory stick is not reused. Guest native text-entry applets are disabled because their routing to the remote screen is not implemented. PPSSPP sends the guest emulator's PCM to the native per-guest queue and keeps the host emulator on normal AudOut. See the recovered audio contract. The console test confirmed audible client playback in the direct-audio build. Start GameShare and join from the client. Open the same game on both screens, then enter its local wireless or Ad Hoc mode. Create a lobby on either console and look for it on the other. If the host had already initialized multiplayer before pairing, restart that game once to select the local route. While GameShare is hosting, PPSSPP runs its built-in discovery service and aemu_postoffice packet relay on IPv4 loopback ports 27314 and 27315. Both cores use the private route automatically with their existing, independently configured PSP MAC addresses. The guest still runs on the host Switch 2, so game packets stay on that console. The route does not use a public relay, Wi-Fi IP address, or UPnP mapping, and it does not change either core's saved network settings. Stopping GameShare closes the listeners. A game already in a lobby may need to leave and re-enter multiplayer after GameShare is restarted. The user reported a successful Tekken session in the first loopback build. The subsequent build keeps each core's original MAC address and passed the ten paired desktop tests. That save-preserving version is tagged switch2-gameshare-multiplayer-baseline (commit 0699365). Its NRO, ZIP and debug ELF are in dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/multiplayer-baseline/. The earlier console run used the temporary-MAC build. Host boot.log, ppsspp.log, native-exit.bin and native-fault.bin live in the experimental app directory. The guest writes guest/ppsspp.log. Native fault/exit records with valid headers are retained as .previous on the next launch. Preserve diagnostics before relaunching after a failure. python3 Switch/tests/run.py python3 Switch/tests/run_gameshare.py python3 Switch/GameShare/sdk/tests/native/run.py python3 Switch/GameShare/sdk/tests/guest_input/run.py python3 Switch/GameShare/sdk/tests/guest_display/run.py git diff --check Actual-source sanitizer tests cover native guest-image sector locations, partial creation, successful retirement, retained uncertain presents and release/range timeouts. SDK tests cover native lifecycle/cancellation, controller parsing/freshness and display ownership. They do not simulate the GPU, native title permissions, GameShare radio behavior or console performance. CPU, GPU, threading and shutdown regression risks require console testing; serialized PSP state layouts are unchanged. The dual-core AArch64 NRO and ZIP built and validated. The symbol audit found 27,173 renamed core-owned symbols and eight guest ABI exports. All 28 SDK native lifecycle scenarios, the input parser/freshness suite and display lifetime suite passed under ASan/UBSan. Six actual-source image-owner scenarios passed (clean, partial create, uncertain present, release timeout, range retirement timeout and unregister failure). Existing JIT publication and dedicated-worker tests also passed. Host regression suites: 102 C++ unit tests passed; 527 executed single-instance PSP cases and ten paired relay scenarios passed. Eleven paired P2P cases remain unrun for the existing missing 127.0.0.2 host loopback alias, causing the aggregate runner's failure status. No executed regression test failed. Console dual-instance rendering, pairing, guest controls/audio and sustained performance still require physical qualification. The initial experimental build produced a system error before the PPSSPP menu. Its boot log reached display configuration; native fault/exit records remained empty. The separate working single-instance installation is unchanged. Pairing and the second emulator have not yet been reached on the console. The SDK bridge is compiled as C++20 separately from the C++17 frontend. Startup checkpoints around Vulkan initialization write startup-stage.bin directly with native flushes. Its four little-endian 64-bit words are magic 0x3254475350505350, stage number, recorder address and system tick. Stages 1–4 cover diagnostics, display configuration, graphics-object construction and error-string construction; stages 10 and 11 bracket InitAPI's initial string assignment. Stages 20 and 21 bracket NativeInit, and 22 precedes window setup. The diagnostic boot marker is comdat-isolation. The native exit recorder also wraps svcBreak (kind 6, reason in the high 32 bits and a readable four-byte detail in the low 32 bits). The final ELF showed that the linker turned a required host string-constructor call into a no-op. GCC used a local C5 signature for the constructor group. Renaming only global symbols let the guest group retain that signature, causing the linker to discard the host copy. The build now renames and checks all 7,351 guest COMDAT groups in addition to the global symbol audit. Disassembly of the corrected ELF confirms that host startup calls its own string constructor and the guest constructor has a distinct address. The console opened the corrected build and started a host game. On the first GameShare attempt, VI2 reached the renderer hook, where a second GSV GPU open failed with 0x200F3. The guest emulator independently reached offscreen Vulkan initialization. The revised uploader uses the existing driver session. The host also joins the SDK thread after terminal states before asking if native resources were retained, so a completed thread alone no longer forces a title restart. Confirm pairing, guest frames and stop/restart on hardware. The shared-session build paired with the client, and the SDK completed cleanup. The client remained black because PPSSPP rejected readback from the guest's offscreen Vulkan presentation before any frame could reach the uploader. Offscreen presentation now declares its transfer-source capability. The copy waits for the color attachment writes and skips frames without an acquired image. A local MoltenVK run cleared three consecutive offscreen frames to different colors and verified every returned RGBA byte. Client presentation and independent input still require a console check. The console confirmed that the host and client can see and control their own PPSSPP screens. Both emulator audio streams were audible from the host. The console-confirmed NRO, matching ELF and installation receipt are saved under dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/dual-screen-controls/. The client was silent in separate-display sessions with both AudOut and Audren. The Audren test boot log confirms the application mix used Audren, the guest received frames and SDK cleanup completed. The launcher NRO was restored to the console-confirmed dual-screen build using the saved SD-card copy. The renderer trial is recorded in commit c5a8716. At the dual-screen checkpoint, both games played through the host. The SDK exposed an application-wide mirroring flag and device-volume configuration. The shipped SDK exports a separate PCM writer and per-guest queue counters. The reusable Moonlight SDK and its PPSSPP copy now expose a PCM callback. Tests of the native worker cover the recovered command layout, the unwritten tail after a partial write, and a failed audio command that leaves video and input running. On November 19, 2026, the console test confirmed sound on the GameShare client. The working build is tagged switch2-gameshare-guest-audio-working (commit 50cd977). The exact installed NRO, SD-card package, matching ELF, SDK archive and build records are saved under dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/guest-audio-working/. For a console rollback, reinstall that NRO as /switch/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare.nro.

candidates.full: Україна отримує масштабне військове посилення напередодні зими! Після чергового засідання у форматі «Рамштайн» союзники оголосили про нові пакети допомоги: винищувачі F-16 від Бельгії, додаткові французькі Mirage, ракети, радари та сотні мільйонів євро на зміцнення протиповітряної оборони. Особливий акцент – на захисті українських міст від російських ракетних і дронових атак. Велика Британія, Данія, Німеччина, Франція та Норвегія оголосили про нові внески на посилення ППО. candidates.full: How can governments build trust in AI? Dr. Laura Gilbert explores AI assurance, secure data sharing and transparency in EY's Data and AI Pioneers. Let’s find the cheapest, simplest solution and measure success against how well it solves that problem – not against generic AI metrics.” That’s one of the main lessons shared by Dr. Laura Gilbert CBE, previously Director of the Incubator for AI at No. 10 Downing Street, in this episode of AI Pioneers. Laura tells Sheena Thompson, EY Government and Infrastructure AI Co-leader, how the Incubator built trust through “competency and intent”. That meant sharing code, evaluations and failures, along with use cases to show it was acting in citizens’ best interests. The conversation also covers the ethical implications of LLMs that are trained on data informed by local cultural norms. And Laura shares her aim of using AI to make the experience of government more human. AI Pioneers is a miniseries featuring speakers from pioneering government organizations identified in EY data and AI reports. Listen in for practical lessons from peers who have successfully moved from ambition to impact – scaling AI to transform their organizations and how they serve citizens.

candidates.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
candidates.summary: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API. When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token co
candidates.full: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API. When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them. How it works To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request. from google import genai client = genai.Client() tools = [ {"type": "tool_search"}, { "type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "description": "Refund an order to the original payment method.", "defer_loading": True, "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}, }, "required": ["order_id", "amount"], }, }, # ... 50+ other deferred functions (leave frequent tools undeferred) ] interaction = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", input="Order A-1042 arrived damaged. Please refund 40 dollars.", tools=tools, ) Inside that single API call, the model searches for issue_refund, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the function_call. All three steps appear in interaction.steps, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions: "steps": [ { "type": "tool_search_call", "id": "tsc_7f2a", "arguments": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]}, "signature": "..." }, { "type": "tool_search_result", "call_id": "tsc_7f2a", "result": [{"type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}], "signature": "..." }, { "type": "function_call", "id": "fc_91c3", "name": "issue_refund", "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40} } ] From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result. There's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the new tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail. Tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn. Tool Retrieval also works with remote MCP servers in the Gemini API. Set defer_loading: true on an mcp_server tool and every tool that server exposes is loaded on demand, so you can connect a large server without listing its tools one by one. How client-side retrieval works If you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the tool_search with "execution": "client" and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose new tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration: tools = [{ "type": "tool_search", "execution": "client", "name": "search_tools", "description": "Search the internal tool registry for functions.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"], }, }] # When the model emits a function_call for "search_tools", # return matching {"type": "function", ...} schemas in function_result: followup = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", previous_interaction_id=interaction.id, tools=tools, input=[{ "type": "function_result", "name": "search_tools", "call_id": step.id, "result": my_registry.search(**step.arguments), }], ) How pricing and supported models work Tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on tool_search adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic. Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API. How to get started - Read the documentation — Full setup guide with examples - Compare Gemini models — Find the best model for your use case - Join the discussion on Discord — Share feedback with the team

candidates.full: «Їду за донечками». У Луцьку чоловік прикрасив вантажівку рожевими кульками та ведмедиками й поїхав зустрічати дружину з пологового — відео Вантажівка повністю у рожевому поїхала зустрічати новонароджених дівчаток (Фото: Аліна Жук/Instagram/Скриншот) Чоловік у Луцьку вирішив оригінально приїхати до пологового, щоб забрати дружину та новонароджених донечок. Відео з кадрами зʼявились у соцмережах й швидко завірусились. Місцеві мешканці знімали момент з різних місць та ракурсів. На відео видно, як вулицями міста їде вантажівка ЗІЛ, прикрашена великою кількістю рожевих кульок, м’якими іграшками та написами: «Їду за донечками». Оригінальний ролик, який опублікував 30-річний мешканець Луцька Петро Корнійчук, набрав понад 1.8 мільйонів переглядів та понад 194 тисячі вподобань. «Такого не те, що Луцьк, а навіть вся Україна не бачила. Супер креативно», — написала у коментарях користувачка Антоніна. Деякі коментатори припустили, як, на їхню думку, можна зустрічати з пологового хлопчиків. Породілля та дружина креативного лучанина розповіла у своєму Instagram, що прикрасити так вантажівку таким чином було мрією її чоловіка.

candidates.full: Українські школярі зможуть опановувати пілотування безпілотників у межах розвитку технологічного спорту. Міністерство молоді та спорту, Федерація технологічного спорту України та F-Drones Simulator підписали меморандум про співпрацю, який передбачає доступ навчальних закладів до спеціалізованого програмного забезпечення протягом наступних п’яти років. У сезоні 2026/2027 технологічний спорт уперше став частиною всеукраїнського проєкту «Пліч-о-пліч». До змагань залучатимуть учнів 5–9 класів, які опановуватимуть пілотування безпілотників у віртуальному середовищі. Кожен заклад освіти, що долучиться до програми, зможе безоплатно встановити симулятор на п’ять комп’ютерів. Федерація також організовуватиме навчання та майстер-класи для педагогів, які готуватимуть шкільні команди до змагань. За словами міністра молоді та спорту Матвія Бідного, партнерство має допомогти дітям, які захоплюються сучасними технологіями, реалізувати свої здібності у спортивних дисциплінах. Перші чотири етапи змагань відбуватимуться дистанційно на платформі F-Drones Simulator. Фіналісти змагатимуться вже з використанням справжніх FPV-дронів на спеціально облаштованій трасі. Команди складатимуться максимум із п’яти учасників. Результати віртуальних перегонів фіксуватиме програмне забезпечення, а до офіційного заліку потраплятимуть польоти, виконані на шкільних комп’ютерах під наглядом учителя. У серпні 2026 року Федерація технологічного спорту спільно з F-Drones організувала перші у світі дистанційні перегони справжніх безпілотників. Дрони перебували на полігоні, тоді як пілоти керували ними в реальному часі за сотні кілометрів. Такий формат відкриває нові можливості для проведення спортивних змагань та залучення молоді до сучасних технологій.

candidates.title: Nvidia Asked to Sell Chips to Companies Tied to Chinese Military and Megaspeed - The New York Times
candidates.summary: Nvidia Asked to Sell Chips to Companies Tied to Chinese Military and Megaspeed Lawmakers released confidential information on Thursday showing that the Commerce Department had approved the sale of more than 800,000 advanced A.I. chips to Chinese companies for the year, as of May 11, including sever
candidates.full: Nvidia Asked to Sell Chips to Companies Tied to Chinese Military and Megaspeed Lawmakers released confidential information on Thursday showing that the Commerce Department had approved the sale of more than 800,000 advanced A.I. chips to Chinese companies for the year, as of May 11, including several firms on a list of Chinese military companies maintained by the Pentagon. The department had received applications to sell more than 3.4 million of the chips to Chinese companies as of that date, lawmakers said. It approved 75,000 artificial intelligence chips for Alibaba, a Chinese A.I. giant that The New York Times reported this week has ties with a military-linked laboratory. The release also showed that Nvidia had submitted an application in April to sell more than 40,000 of its advanced H200 chips to a company tied to Megaspeed and Alice Huang, the executive who U.S. intelligence has concluded was a Chinese asset who had an affair with the former Nvidia chief executive. The company — New Century Lettall Data Service — is part of a network of Chinese companies with ties to Megaspeed and Ms. Huang. Its historical ownership traces back in part to an investment firm controlled by Ms. Huang’s sister, where Kang Wei, whom Ms. Huang often introduced as her husband, was also executive director. The Commerce Department also approved 150,000 chips for the Chinese tech conglomerate Tencent and its subsidiaries; 43,000 for Baidu, another Chinese A.I. firm; and 4,000 for BYD, a carmaker, the lawmakers said. They were Nvidia’s H200 chips and the equivalent from the chip maker AMD, the MI325X. The lawmakers, from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, took special note of the Commerce Department’s approval of sales to the companies Maginfra, Beijing New Matrix Information Technologies and Aivres Systems. The committee cited reporting by The New York Times that had raised questions about those firms because of their ties to sanctioned entities and noted that many of the license requests from Nvidia had listed the companies as entities that might install the systems in data centers. Two Times reports first raised concerns about the firms in September and October, saying that Aivres was the subsidiary of a sanctioned Chinese firm that had exported billions of dollars of advanced Nvidia chips to Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Nvidia scandal. Times reporters also visited the China offices of Maginfra and New Matrix and found them to be empty. No one present had heard of the firms, and scant information existed about them online, raising questions about whether they really existed. The revelations that Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, was having an affair with Ms. Huang, along with a second woman at Nvidia, forced him to step down last week. The Justice and Commerce Departments said this week that Megaspeed was under criminal investigation for potentially smuggling chips into China. The incident has sparked criticism from lawmakers that the Trump administration, and the Commerce Department in particular, did too little to police the flow of sensitive technology to China. Officials both in the administration and on Capitol Hill have criticized the department for maintaining close ties to Nvidia, which it is charged with regulating. The Commerce Department has defended its processes, saying that it closely follows national security regulations. Every Nvidia and AMD application also stated that the proposed transfer posed a low risk of diversion, the committee’s release said. John Rizzo, a spokesman for Nvidia, said that all of the company’s shipments were legal and authorized by the government, and that, despite receiving some licenses, Nvidia had already stopped shipping H200s to China. Nvidia “did not and will not” ship an H200 to the company linked to Megaspeed, or any other company, he said. A spokeswoman for AMD said the company complied with applicable U.S. laws and regulations and had a rigorous process to ensure compliance. A spokesman for the Commerce Department said the disclosure was evidence of the department’s transparency with Congress about licensing activity. Licensing decisions are the product of deliberation and consultation among multiple U.S. government agencies, he said. President Trump approved the sale of the H200 to China in December under unusual conditions. He required the chips, which are assembled in Taiwan, to be routed through the United States on their way to China, so that the government could collect a 25 percent tariff on their value and perform a security check. Wary of the arrangement and eager to promote its own technology, the Chinese government ended up approving few purchases from its firms. Nvidia said in its earnings this week that it would halt sales of its H200 chips to China, though it did not give a reason for the move. In its statement, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said that withholding the information was “contrary to the national interest.” The committee plans to hold hearings next month with both Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, and his deputy Jeff Kessler, who has had a special role in approving license applications. Representative Brian Mast, a Florida Republican and chairman of the committee, called Maginfra and New Matrix “fake companies,” and said that if the Commerce Department granted approvals to the firms, “obviously that is of tremendous concern to us,” he said. Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Democrat of New York, said that the public deserved to know how decisions to sell technology to China were made, and that Congress needed to “conduct rigorous oversight.” “Over the past month, the administration’s handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk,” he said. Ana Swanson covers trade and international economics for The Times and is based in Washington. She has been a journalist for more than a decade. Cecilia Kang reports on technology and regulatory policy for The Times from Washington. She has written about technology for over two decades.
